item.text: The persistent-storage check is compiling RocksDB from source in its own feature/dependency configuration, so I’m letting that finish rather than treating the delay as a result. In parallel, the source contract is clear: `write_atomically` mutates both `write_batch` and `next_log_key` incrementally and only clears them after the final `db.write`, so any serialization error can strand or later commit a partial transaction.

item.text: The persistent-storage reproduction confirmed a tenth defect: a failed atomic transaction leaked its already-queued append. The failed call immediately reported `len_after_failure=1`; a subsequent unrelated write then committed that append, despite the `Storage::write_atomically` all-or-none contract.

item.text:
Audit continued and now has ten confirmed defects. Full evidence and reproduction commands are in [report.md](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-17_22-19-35-omnipaxos-baseline/work/report.md).

The two highest-impact findings are:

- **Decided snapshot corruption during delta synchronization.** [internal_storage.rs](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-17_22-19-35-omnipaxos-baseline/work/omnipaxos/src/storage/internal_storage.rs:318) assigns the new leader’s decided index before building the receiver’s delta-snapshot base, incorporating obsolete accepted entries. The deterministic reproduction produced `[1,2,3,6,7,4,5]` instead of `[1,2,3,4,5]`: [audit_sync_delta_snapshot.rs](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-17_22-19-35-omnipaxos-baseline/work/omnipaxos/tests/audit_sync_delta_snapshot.rs).
- **Persistent atomic writes leak failed transactions.** [persistent_storage.rs](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-17_22-19-35-omnipaxos-baseline/work/omnipaxos_storage/src/persistent_storage.rs:278) retains queued operations and advances `next_log_key` when a later operation fails. A subsequent unrelated transaction committed the leaked append: [main.rs](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-17_22-19-35-omnipaxos-baseline/work/persistent_check/src/main.rs).

Other confirmed findings cover sparse-ID trim failure, cross-epoch ballot ordering, non-increasing reconfiguration IDs, runtime subscription duplication and event-loop blocking, feature-unification compilation failure, zero-node-ID arithmetic panic, and a zero batch-flush timeout that never fires.

All shipped default-feature core and runtime tests passed, including the four normally ignored recovery tests. A randomized 2,654-proposal loss/duplication/reordering run found no decided-prefix conflict. The snapshot defect was independently corroborated by intermittent failures of the shipped `sync_full_test`, with the same corrupted snapshot signature.
